info.title: ShopFloor Twin MES API
info.description: API of the MES (Phases 4 and 5): equipment with current state, state intervals, telemetry series, shift totals, the plant clock, OEE per hour and shift, shift instances, reason codes, downtime records and the loss Pareto; alarm occurrences and alarm KPIs per hour and shift (Phase 6); one write, downtime coding (#121), with its audit. No authentication yet (Phase 7): writes are guarded (ADR-0023: Origin of this host, Sec-Fetch-Site, application/json, 16 KiB, a global rate limit, MES_WRITES=off answers 405) and audited as unauthenticated; bound to loopback by default. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details. Push: WebSocket at /api/v1/ws (see docs/api/realtime.md).

type.description: Always about:blank: the status says it all

Problem.description: An error (RFC 9457 problem details), served as application/problem+json

put.summary: Codes one downtime record: replaces its codings (splits, comment, who)
put.description: Each segment is a time range [from, to) inside the record with an active reason (not UNCODED); segments must not overlap; an empty list clears the codings. Time without a coding keeps the auto reason. `version` is the record’s `version` as read: it belongs to the coding set of the (equipment, epoch), and a mismatch is 409. `codedBy` is free text, recorded as unauthenticated. Audited; reasons never change OEE, only the Pareto and the reason view. Writes need an Origin of this host (or allowlisted), `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` when sent, and application/json (ADR-0023).

get.summary: The shift report: OEE, downtime, production, alarms and handover notes
get.description: Computed on read (ADR-0025): the OEE section is the body of /shifts/{date}/{shift}/oee; the downtime Pareto by reason sums to the own and external availability loss, with the ten longest records and the uncoded time; production per machine from the OEE inputs and finished parts (the line’s last machine); per position and the plant the alarm KPIs of the shift bucket (equal to /alarms/kpi) and the top 5 bad actors; the handover notes with their history. `final` once every input is final; `revision.inputs` counts input revisions after that, `revision.content` note writes and recodes (recoding never changes OEE). `generatedAt` and `asOf` are for a printout.

post.summary: Shelves an alarm point for a time of plant time
post.description: ISA-18.2 shelves a point, not an occurrence: its occurrences leave the active list and keep their states; KPIs count every raise anyway. `durationMs` runs in plant time, 1 minute to maxShelveMs (alarms.yaml, 8 hours; longer is 422): `until` = the plant clock now + duration; once the plant clock passes it, the MES unshelves the point itself (audited `expire`, actor system), and a newer epoch ends the shelf (`epoch-ended`). Shelving a shelved point replaces its shelf. `version` is the shelf’s as read (0 for a point never shelved): a mismatch is 409. Writes need an Origin of this host (or allowlisted), `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` when sent, and application/json (ADR-0023); `actor` is free text, audited as unauthenticated in alarms.alarm_transition with wall time, plant time and the request id. Operator actions never change alarm KPIs or their revisions (every raise counts).
